title: Add cross-stage cost flare visualization and observability playbook
author: Priya Menon
description: Motivation: When investigating cost spikes we frequently saw noisy, stage-local metrics (tokenization, model_forward, kv_fetch, decode) that were individually unhelpful. This PR introduces a cross-stage visualization ('Cost Flare') that aligns per-stage token-cost and latency signals to surface correlated flares across the inference pipeline and provides an SRE playbook with automated alert suggestions to speed triage. What changed: 1) A new dashboard JSON for the Cost Flare visualization that aggregates rollups from per-stage telemetry and renders a radial heat/flare view to highlight stages with simultaneous cost/latency deviations; 2) A lightweight cost-annotation agent (telemetry/cost_annotator.go) that tags spans with stage_cost_breakdown and emits compact provenance keys so the dashboard can do low-cardinality joins; 3) An auto-suggester (telemetry/thresholds/auto_suggester.py) that examines correlated anomalies across stages and proposes an alerting bundle (thresholds + priority) in the console; 4) A playbook runbook (observability/playbooks/cost_flare_playbook.md) with reproducible triage steps and recommended SLO actions. Backwards compatibility: All new fields are optional and safely ignored by older dashboards; the annotator falls back to emitting legacy token-cost labels if per-stage data is unavailable. Testing & rollout: Unit tests and integration tests added; deployed to staging with a 24h synthetic replay; gradual canary rollout to production with a kill-switch metric. Security & perf: The annotator operates asynchronously and adds a bounded amount of metadata (<= 128 bytes per invocation) to avoid increasing downstream costs. Links: ENG-1190 for design notes, SUP-2213 for customer incident that motivated this work.
